result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers make the same core recommendation: Select as the default mode, Paint as a separate armed mode, and Record as a button rather than a mode. A gives more show-relevant detail: an indicator that doesn't depend on color alone in a dim booth, each paint stroke as one undo step, a Record button that shows the cue number and asks for a cue-specific confirmation before overwriting, a rehearsal test with deliberate distractions, and an open question about whether paint changes the stage immediately. B is shorter and adds a useful show-lock idea, and it names the cost of switching modes more directly, but its indicator and undo guidance are less specific. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers reach the same sound design: Select as the default, Paint as an armed tool that is clearly shown on screen, and Record as a separate button that asks for confirmation. Both also explain clearly why the timing-based gesture option fails. B is stronger on show-time safety: it says not to rely on color alone in a dim booth, gives every action a route that doesn't need a gesture, and puts status in a fixed bar. It also ties its strictness to whether painting changes the stage immediately or only edits a preview. A is tighter but less thorough.
